pois.name: GINZA SIX
pois.description: Ginza's premier luxury flagship — 13 floors of over 240 high-end boutiques (Louis Vuitton, Céline, Valentino, Dior, Hermès), restaurants, and one of Tokyo's best rooftop gardens. The centrepiece is a 6-storey atrium with a 30-metre mobile by Jeff Koons. Japan's largest luxury department store.

pois.name: Kabuki-za Theatre
pois.description: The home of traditional kabuki theatre in Tokyo. The current building (2013) is the fifth on this site — its neo-Momoyama architectural style (ornate green roof curves, white facade) is one of the most recognised in Japan. Single-act tickets (hitomaku-mi) allow casual visitors without booking a full day.

pois.name: Ginza Chuo-dori
pois.description: The central boulevard of Ginza — closed to traffic every weekend afternoon as a 'pedestrian paradise'. Lined with flagships of Hermès (Renzo Piano, the tilework building), Cartier, Apple Ginza, Uniqlo, and Mikimoto (the pearl jeweller that has been here since 1899). The de facto fashion axis of Tokyo.

pois.name: Itoya Stationery
pois.description: The world's most famous stationery shop — 12 floors of paper, pens, and design objects at the corner of Chuo-dori and Mitsu-dori. A Ginza institution since 1904. The 2015 redesign by Klein Dytham architecture includes a rooftop farm growing ingredients for the in-house café.

pois.name: Ginza Art District
pois.description: The side streets above Ginza 8-chome host Tokyo's highest concentration of serious contemporary art galleries — Wako Museum, Shinwa Art Auction, Gallery Koyanagi, and over 30 others in the art alley network. Most are free to enter and change shows monthly.
